headline: Majors stuck below trend, funding turns negative on alts, whales split between withdrawal and accumulation
paragraphs: All seven major assets remain below their 200-day moving averages with no golden crosses in place. Bitcoin at 64,197 sits 48.5% below its 12-month high of 124,739, Ethereum 60.8% below 4,817, and Solana 69.3% below 247.6. The regime is defined not by uptrend but by sideways recovery within a deeply retraced range. Over the last seven days, Bitcoin has gained 2.22% and Ethereum 2.48%, but these are bounces within a bear structure, not reversals of it. The tape reads as relief rally, not regime shift.

Momentum is mixed and telling a story of fatigue in the recovery. Bitcoin's RSI sits exactly at 50.1, the neutral line, with MACD above signal but fading into overbought territory that usually precedes pullback. Ethereum's RSI is 52.4 and MACD is below signal, a bearish divergence even as price ticked up 1.02% in the 24 hours. Binance stands apart with RSI at 66.5, genuinely overbought, yet still below its 200-day line. XRP is the clearest warning: RSI at 34.5 with MACD below signal and price down 0.42% on the day, down 5.08% over seven days. The asset classes are not moving in lockstep. BTC and ETH are grind higher on fading momentum. Smaller caps and alts are rolling over.

Derivatives positioning reveals crowding at both ends. Bitcoin's funding rate is 0.0065% per 8 hours (annualized 7.1%), paid by longs to shorts, and the long/short ratio is 1.35 to 1. That is moderately bullish positioning but not extreme. Ethereum funding is tighter at 0.0016% per 8 hours (1.8% annual) with a 1.78 long-to-short ratio, showing heavier long conviction but lighter absolute cost to carry. Open interest remains substantial: 2.08 billion in BTC perpetuals, 1.35 billion in ETH. The real signal is in the alts. Solana funding turned negative at minus 0.0029% per 8 hours (minus 3.2% annual), shorts are being paid to hold, and the long/short ratio is 2.0 to 1, a crowded long structure. XRP funding is at minus 0.0044% per 8 hours (minus 4.8% annual) with an extreme long/short ratio of 3.69 to 1. These are one-directional bets, and funding is now punishing them. Liquidations in the last 24 hours show 919 BTC longs liquidated for 9.57 million dollars against 465,071 for shorts; the imbalance is stark and points to long positioning being tested.

Whale flows display a tension worth noting. Over the 24-hour window, 16.8 million dollars in net value moved off exchanges, nominally a withdrawal signal. But beneath that sits a split: Ethereum saw 56.17 million move off exchanges (cold storage accumulation), while Bitcoin saw 39.34 million move onto exchanges (institutional and retail selling or rebalancing). The biggest single moves onto exchanges were USDT 139.96 million to Bitfinex and BTC 90.3 million to Coinbase Institutional on one side; the biggest off were USDT 169.89 million from Bitfinex and BTC 128.87 million from Kraken on the other. These are not coordinated whale moves but rather opposing flows: one group reducing exchange exposure, another adding. The weekly trend is volatile. The past four weeks show outflows of 239.24 million, then inflows of 1.116 billion, 1.111 billion, and most recently outflows of 402.08 million. There is no persistence. Stablecoin float sits at 305.4 billion, down 1.38% over thirty days, a slow drain of dry powder.

Sentiment is locked at 29 (Fear), the lower bound of a narrow 30-day range of 22 to 33. The crowd is fearful and has been, consistently. Yet Bitcoin's 24-hour move was up 0.44%, Ethereum up 1.02%, and BNB up 2.12%. The tape is grinding higher while the mood stays gloomy. This is neither explosive accumulation nor capitulation; it is a controlled, low-volume recovery in a fear regime. ETF flows confirm the hesitation. Bitcoin spot ETFs saw an outflow of 144.6 million on August 10, the latest date. Over the last five sessions, they took in 550.6 million, but the same-direction count is only 1, meaning yesterday reversed a multi-day trend. Ethereum is similar: a 14.6 million outflow on the 10th against a five-session net of 241.0 million.

Watch three conditions to signal a tape shift. First, a reclaim of the 200-day moving average by Bitcoin, Ethereum, or the majority of the sample would break the bear structure. Second, funding on Solana and XRP flipping positive would signal shorts covering and alts bottoming; negative funding punishing longs is a ceiling. Third, whale flows: a reversion to consistent outflows over the next two to three weeks would mark genuine cold storage accumulation, separating noise from intent. Until then, the tape reads as relief within a long-term bear, fear sentiment masking modest accumulation, and derivatives positioning that is crowded on the long side of smaller caps. That is volatile ground.
